figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. The eﬀects of plumbagin on cell proliferative inhibition and colony formation in melanoma A375.S2. (a) Cell proliferative
inhibition eﬀect of plumbagin in A375.S2 cells. (b) Inﬂuence of A375.S2 on the number of colony-forming cells, as evaluated by clonogenic
assay. Cell growth inhibition activity of plumbagin was assessed by XTT. For colony-forming assay, the clonogenic assay was performed
as described in Section 2. Results are expressed as the percentage of cell proliferation relative to the proliferation of control. The data
shown are the mean from three independent experiments. Each value is the mean ± SD of three determinations. The asterisk indicates a
signiﬁcant diﬀerence between control and plumbagin-treated cells, as analyzed by Dunnett’s test (p < 0.05).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Plumbagin induced apoptosis through the initiation of the mitochondrial pathway. (a) The DNA fragmentation of A375.S2
induced by plumbagin was determined by electrophoresis assay. Quantitative evaluations of TUNEL assay by ﬂow cytometry (b) and
ﬂuorescence microscope (c). (d) The expression level of Bcl-2 family proteins. The activation of caspase-9 (e), caspase-7 (f) and caspase-3
(g) in A375.S2 cells. For (a), cells were treated with various concentrations of plumbagin for 48 h or 20 lM plumbagin for indicated times,
and then DNA fragmentation was assessed by agarose gel electrophoresis. For (b) and (c), TUNEL-positive cells were examined by ﬂow
cytometry, and were visible through ﬂuorescence microscope. For (d), the Bcl-2 expression levels of 20 lM plumbagin-treated A375.S2
cells were determined by Western blot. Caspase-9 was assessed by Caspase-9 activity assay kit. Caspase-7 and caspase-3 was assessed by
CaspSELECTTM Caspase-7 and -3 Immunoassay Kits. Each value is the mean ± SD of three determinations. The asterisk indicates a
signiﬁcant diﬀerence between control and plumbagin-treated cells, as analyzed by Dunnett’s test (p < 0.05).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Plumbagin increased the activation of ASK1, JNK, and ERK1/2. (a) The eﬀect of plumbagin on the activation of ASK1 and
MAPK. (b) Plumbagin increased the activity of JNK and ERK1/2. Phosphorylated and unphosphorylated protein levels were assessed by
Western blot assay. The JNK and ERK1/2 activity was determined using JNK and ERK1/2 Activity kit from Cell Signaling Technology
(Beverly, MA) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Results shown are representative of three independent experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. The role of ROS on plumbagin-mediated JNK activation and apoptosis. Antioxidant agents inhibited plumbagin-mediated JNK
activation (a), and caspase-9 activation (b) and apoptosis (c). Cells were pre-treated with catalase (1000 U/mL) or vitamin C (100 lM) for
1 h, then 20 lM plumbagin was added and incubated for speciﬁc times (3 h for JNK activity, 36 h for caspase-9, and 48 h for apoptosis
assay). The activation of JNK was measured by Western blot assay. The induction of apoptosis was determined by TUNEL analysis. Each
value is the mean ± SD of three determinations. The asterisk indicates a signiﬁcant diﬀerence between two test groups, as analyzed by
Dunnett’s test (p < 0.05).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. The role of JNK and ERK1/2 on plumbagin-triggered mitochondrial apoptotis pathway. (a) The eﬀects of SB600125 and PD98059
on plumbagin-mediated JNK and ERK1/2 activation. (b) The eﬀects of SP600125 and PD98059 on plumbagin-mediated cell cycle arrest.
Both of SP600125 and PD98059 inhibits plumbagin-mediated Bax upregulation (c), caspase-9 activation (d) and apoptosis (e). Cells were
pre-treated with SP600125 (20 lM) or PD98059 (20 lM) for 1 h, then 20 lM plumbagin was added and incubated for speciﬁc times (12 h
for Bax, and 36 h for caspase-9 and 48 h for apoptosis assay). Each value is the mean ± SD of three determinations. The asterisk indicates
a signiﬁcant diﬀerence between two test groups, as analyzed by Dunnett’s test (p < 0.05).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 8. Plumbagin inhibits growth of A375.S2 in nude mice. (a) Mean of tumor volume measured at the indicated number of days after
implant. (b) No sign of toxicity, as judged by parallel monitoring of body weight and tissue sections of lungs, livers, and kidneys, was
observed in plumbagin-treated mice. (c) Plumbagin induced apoptotic cell death in A375.S2 xenograft. Animals bearing pre-established
tumors (n = 12 per group) were dosed daily for 28 days with i.p. injections of plumbagin (2 mg/kg/d) or vehicle. During the 28-day
treatment, tumor volumes were estimated using measurements taken by external calipers (mm3). The apoptosis was determined by
TUNEL assay. Each value is the mean ± SD of three determinations. The asterisk indicates a signiﬁcant diﬀerence between control and
plumbagin-treated cells, as analyzed by Dunnett’s test (p < 0.05).
